subject.title: [Feature]: Support Anthropic native server-side tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution)

question: What Anthropic server-tool contract should OpenClaw support for web_search, web_fetch, code_execution/PTC, and allowed_callers, and what opt-in, billing, replay, and security defaults must gate it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but provider-hosted code execution and delegated tool access change tool availability, billing, transcript replay, and security boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Plugin-owned opt-in contract
options.body: Add an Anthropic plugin/provider contract for selected server tools, default risky execution or billing paths off, preserve current client tools unless explicitly replaced, and require docs plus live provider proof.

options.title: Web search first
options.body: Sponsor only the narrower Anthropic native web_search provider first while keeping this broad tracker open for web_fetch, code_execution/PTC, allowed_callers, and replay semantics.

options.title: Decline provider-hosted execution
options.body: Support only read-only Anthropic server tools for now and reject code_execution/PTC until maintainers explicitly accept delegated provider execution as an OpenClaw capability.

recommendation.title: Plugin-owned opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Add an Anthropic plugin/provider contract for selected server tools, default risky execution or billing paths off, preserve current client tools unless explicitly replaced, and require docs plus live provider proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the latest visible issue-review context and broad recent history across the affected Anthropic provider, plugin-boundary, and config surfaces.
